small_guidance:
- The post-conv fused kernel is already cheap; the ConvTranspose2d dominates. Tuning BLOCK_HW/BLOCK_C of the softmax kernel further will not move fast_p meaningfully. If staying small, try BLOCK_HW=256 with num_warps=4 and persistent rows (one program per (n, hw_tile) loading C=128 in a single tile) to remove the cdiv math.
- Fold the bias add into the softmax sum path (compute `sigmoid((softmax + bias) * s)` directly from exp_x/inv_sum without rematerializing) — already done; minor win available by precomputing `bias * scaling_factor` on host once per forward.
- Ensure conv output is in channels_last so the C reduction is contiguous; currently C-stride is HW=16384 making softmax loads strided.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose2d` with a custom Triton scatter-add (or input-major gather) kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output spatial tile), iterating over (IC, kh, kw) with stride/padding/output_padding index math. This is the dominant cost (~12ms baseline) and the only path to fast_p > 1.
- Fuse the softmax+bias+scale+sigmoid epilogue into the conv-transpose kernel only if the kernel is structured per-output-element with full C reduction; otherwise keep softmax as a separate pass over the conv output but launch it on a channels_last layout produced directly by the conv kernel.
- Consider the gather formulation: output[n, oc, oh, ow] = sum over (ic, kh, kw) of input[n, ic, ih, iw] * weight[ic, oc, kh, kw], where ih = (oh + padding - kh)/stride when divisible. This avoids atomics and maps cleanly to a GEMM-tiled Triton kernel with BLOCK_OC×BLOCK_OHW tiles and K = IC*kh*kw.
